Use the patch tool to replace the 'Optional Dependencies' section of docs/system-dependencies.rst with a 'Python Extras' section (heading underlined with '-------------') describing optional extras, followed by a 'System Packages' heading, keeping the '===================' title underline.
expected: The patch applies and the file contains the new sections.
defect: The patch tool rejects the patch with `Invalid patch: invalid patch format: extra ======= marker found in updated content` because the RST underline `===================` is taken for a divider.
Root cause: FIXED UPSTREAM IN https://github.com/gptme/gptme/pull/1203 (commit b201c91ce334b4e44b370f3d0b2803f5214897ff). Patch parsing in gptme/tools/patch.py split the ORIGINAL/UPDATED block at the ======= divider and then rejected the patch if the updated part still contained `"\n======="`; that substring test also matches any longer run of '=' at a line start, such as an RST title underline, so valid patches were refused. PR #1203 replaces it with the regex `\n=======(?!=)`, which matches only exactly seven '='. Ships in v0.32.0; the pinned revision contains it.

_meta.notes: The pinned revision 0c131bb0d642fcdd1edb2c6fec02eccfe7f71a07 (v0.35.1) already contains the fix, but no release that lacks the fix provides the gptme-acp entry point (gptme-acp first appears in pyproject.toml at commit 75d94dd34, 2025-12-18, first tagged in v0.31.1.dev20260227 / v0.32.0), so version_choice stays 'pinned'. Because the faulty code no longer exists at the tested revision, 'fault location' is left empty and the pre-fix location is recorded here instead: gptme/tools/patch.py Patch parsing (`if "\n=======" in modified:`) at b201c91ce^. The reporter's file is the gptme docs file; step 1 creates an equivalent .rst file. Depends on the model including the underline inside the ORIGINAL/UPDATED blocks.
